The October12 capture includes COMPLETED count32,194 and unique_count32,193 in one daily period. Its full source retains12 workflow links,61 daily periods,37 hourly periods and2 hourly rolling periods.

Every native record, series and period remains in the complete JSON and portable handover. A later capture retains its newly returned observations as another edition.

### Explicit continuation and coverage

The deployed response to `since=1h&state=COMPLETED&limit=2` returned two items and omitted `nextkey`. A subsequent actual GET using its last retained `payload_id` in the documented `nextkey` field returned two distinct earlier records. Both requests and connector carriers are preserved in the receiving example.

The capture status and the coverage of its latest native page are separate:

| Native response | Retained coverage |
|---|---|
| A native nextkey is present | `MORE_NATIVE_PAGES`; the original provider follows that cursor |
| Items are present with no cursor | `NO_NATIVE_CURSOR_RETURNED`; the operator can review explicit continuation |
| An empty items page has no cursor | `EMPTY_NATIVE_PAGE`; that request observed an empty tail |

**Continue from last native payload** pins the latest retained capture SHA-256, records the last actual payload identifier as the operator's selected cursor, and executes the GET through the same provider and edition lease. It retains the workflow, state, duration and page size. The selection origin is `operator-last-native-payload-id`; an actual response cursor retains `response-nextkey`.

**Prepare continuation for an external capture** performs the same selection and leaves its exact request ready for **Import response**. Repeating the operation ID reconciles that original selection. A changed source page or previously used cursor is rejected before dispatch.

Cirrus evaluates relative `since` at each request. Every selected duration and original request/capture time is retained, making the windows used during a long traversal visible. The UI shows saved pages, returned/limit values, coverage, continuation history and the next request together.

This uses the original per-attempt request/body store, source fingerprint, job state, native lease, export and receiving mechanisms. The complete source package travels with its imported responses.

Find and use files delivered by the original SF88 buyer. The library connects
cross-intent content search, source inspection, exact file downloads and durable
analyst reviews in one private workspace. Its native CLI and browser share the
same implementation and SQLite index. Node 22.16 or newer supplies the runtime;
the library adds no external dependencies.

## Open your existing inbox

Use the installed original inbox command. Choose a separate private state
directory and explicitly declare the directories containing your delivered files.


From a source checkout, replace `starforge inbox library` with

Open the private loopback URL printed by the command. Choose **Refresh source**,

Snapshot mode consumes this exact JSON array. Its refresh reads the current file

## Review and reuse

Search matches words across source labels and the verified text prefix. Results
show `COMPLETE`, `PREFIX` or `BINARY` coverage with explicit indexed-byte counts.
JSON is displayed as original decoded text, preserving large integer literals
and formatting. Seller-supplied HTML and scripts are displayed as text.

A completed refresh publishes one complete generation. Search remains available
against the prior generation during another refresh. Cancellation preserves that
prior generation. After a process interruption, the next scan detects a stopped
same-host writer and reclaims its derived staging generation; Linux also checks
process start identity to distinguish PID reuse. An active writer continues to
own its current scan. The original inbox, delivery files and payment records stay
under their existing implementations.

Every preview hashes the complete current file against the original delivery's
size and SHA-256. Downloads stream a private verified copy of those same bytes,
so later changes to the original path cannot change the download. POSIX temporary
copies are unlinked while open and reclaimed by the operating system if the
process ends. The browser receives a short-lived, single-use file transfer and
streams through its native download facility. Four file transfers may be prepared
or active concurrently. Failed and partial deliveries remain visible as
`INCOMPLETE`; changed, missing and outside-root files remain `UNAVAILABLE`.

Analyst reviews use append-only revisions and explicit expected revisions.
Replaying the same operation ID and payload returns its saved result after a lost
reply. Concurrent edits produce `ANNOTATION_REVISION_CONFLICT` and retain the
browser draft. **Load saved review** retrieves the current saved version. The
revision history can copy a prior review into the draft for another explicit save.
**Export review** includes current source references and every saved review
revision, including reviews whose resource has since left the current inbox.

The displayed buyer status and HTTP status are copied from the original outcome.
The file's verification and the analyst's notes occupy their own fields. Request
URL query strings, fragments and user information are omitted from the derived
view. The original intent ID and config SHA-256 identify the source request.

```sh
starforge inbox library scan --state /private/buyer-library
starforge inbox library search --state /private/buyer-library --query 'copper conduit'
starforge inbox library search --state /private/buyer-library --starred true --offset 0 --limit 50
```

Output files are create-only in an existing private directory. CLI annotations
use `annotate --id RESOURCE_ID --annotation /private/note.json`, where the JSON

```js
import { openLibrary } from './library.mjs';
const library = await openLibrary({
  state: '/private/buyer-library', kind: 'inbox',
  source: '/private/buyer-inbox', roots: ['/private/downloads'],

try {

  const resource = matches.items[0];
```

# Enforce an API's response contract before settlement

The existing OpenAPI import and SF30 upstream seller can now carry the original
operation's response promises into its delivery path. A merchant backend's JSON
can be syntactically valid while missing required fields, using the wrong value
types, or returning an undocumented successful status. With a response contract,
the existing upstream handler rejects that result before SF30 calls its native
post-handler settlement step.

This is an opt-in extension of the existing seller. It uses the same OpenAPI
reference resolver and 3.0 compatibility adapter, the original SF25 schema
validator, the same backend transport, and the unchanged SF30 payment lifecycle.

## Export a runnable merchant configuration

Prepare the existing OpenAPI JSON, explicit operation selections with merchant
payment terms, service bindings naming application handlers, and ordinary
[upstream bindings](../sf30-seller-sdk/UPSTREAM.md). Give distinct OpenAPI operations
distinct handler names. Then run:

```sh
I=stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf61-openapi-seller-import
S=stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk

node "$I/cli.mjs" \
  --spec /private/merchant/openapi.json \
  --config /private/merchant/selections.json \
  --service-bindings /private/merchant/service-bindings.json \
  --upstream-bindings /private/merchant/upstreams.json \
  --out /private/merchant/release-001

node "$S/upstream-serve.mjs" \
  --config /private/merchant/release-001/seller-service.json \
  --upstreams /private/merchant/release-001/upstreams.json --check

node "$S/upstream-serve.mjs" \
  --config /private/merchant/release-001/seller-service.json \
  --upstreams /private/merchant/release-001/upstreams.json
```

The export directory must be new. It contains the original offers and seller
configuration plus `upstreams.json`, with a compiled `responseContract` on each
selected upstream handler. The manifest records the exact OpenAPI bytes,
upstream input/output and response compiler/runtime hashes. The output retains
the merchant's backend mapping and environment-variable **names**; export never
reads environment credentials or calls the backend. Native `--check` performs
the existing transport, route and actual environment preflight.

Files use mode `0600` inside a `0700` directory. Keep the export private: it
contains API schemas and backend configuration. Existing `responseFile` assets
are bundled as before. Original offer metadata, request schemas, payment terms,
static responses and admission options are preserved. Export refuses unused or
missing upstream bindings and refuses to overwrite a manually supplied contract.

The last command starts the existing challenge-only service. Use the original
`--facilitator` setup when the merchant is ready to enable its native payment
runtime. `--allow-loopback-upstream` remains required for a same-machine HTTP
backend. These flags and their meanings are unchanged.

## Runtime behavior

| Backend result | Existing seller behavior with a contract |
| --- | --- |
| Declared successful status, JSON media type and matching schema | Returns the original decoded bytes to native SF30 settlement; releases them only after native success |
| JSON violates the matching schema | Sanitized HTTP 502 `UPSTREAM_RESPONSE_CONTRACT_SCHEMA`; original cancellation path |
| Successful status has no exact, `2XX`, or `default` definition | HTTP 502 `UPSTREAM_RESPONSE_CONTRACT_STATUS`; original cancellation path |
| JSON media type does not match the selected response definition | HTTP 502 `UPSTREAM_RESPONSE_CONTRACT_MEDIA_TYPE`; original cancellation path |
| Declared HEAD, 204 or 205 | Preserves bodyless HTTP semantics; no invented empty JSON response |
| Backend 4xx/5xx, redirect, timeout, malformed or oversized response | Existing SF30 upstream failure behavior |

Exact status definitions take precedence over `2XX`, which takes precedence over
`default`. A broad fallback cannot relax an explicit `200` schema. Media types
are compared without parameters and case-insensitively at runtime. The importer
accepts explicit lowercase `application/json` and concrete `application/...+json`
keys, such as `application/problem+json`; it does not treat a wildcard MIME range
as equivalent to a declared JSON representation.

Response validation occurs after the one backend invocation and before the
original seller's post-handler settlement call. Some native payment schemes may
have already performed a pre-handler settlement; cancellation/refund handling
remains the native SDK's responsibility. This feature does not promise that every
failure avoids every network payment, nor does it undo a mutating backend request.
Use the existing [backend side-effect contract](../sf30-seller-sdk/UPSTREAM.md#failure-and-side-effect-contract).

Failures expose a stable error code and upstream status only. They do not return
the backend payload, private schema path, credentials or validation diagnostics.
Existing per-binding failure telemetry includes these ordinary handler failures.

## Supported contract

OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1 local reference objects and schemas follow the original
importer's rules. In particular, 3.0 `nullable` and exclusive numeric bounds
retain their original meaning. Runtime uses SF25's supported JSON Schema 2020-12
vocabulary: object properties/required/additional properties, arrays/items,
types, enum/const, supported composition, string length and numeric bounds.
Unknown assertions fail export or startup. References are resolved before a
schema is embedded under the validator's response envelope. The shared resolver
removes OpenAPI 3.1 discriminator hints, which cannot change JSON Schema
validation, while retaining all original compositions and assertions.

All explicitly declared success responses and `default` are compiled. Error
status definitions remain the upstream adapter's existing failure path. Empty
content requires HEAD or explicit 204/205. HEAD/204/205 never acquire a payload
merely because OpenAPI describes a representation. Response header assertions,
links, callbacks, non-JSON encodings, recursive references and unsupported
schema assertions are outside this contract. It does not certify a backend,
seller identity, result accuracy, business transaction or chain settlement.

For programmatic use, pass `responseContract` to the existing
`createUpstreamHandler`, or place it on an original upstream binding. It requires
JSON mode; manually supplied unresolved schema references fail startup. Ordinary
bindings without this field retain their existing behavior.

## Focused native integration

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf61-openapi-seller-import/response-contract-acceptance.mjs
```

One journey exports the real original source, starts an actual local backend and
the original SF30 seller, and exercises mismatch cancellation, byte-preserving
valid delivery, status/media rejection, bodyless responses and unchanged
challenge-only behavior. A controlled native-compatible collaborator makes the
existing cancellation/settlement calls observable. It is a runtime integration
check, not a Stellar network transaction. No hosted Actions are required.

Protocol sources: [OpenAPI 3.1.1 Responses Object](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.1.html#responses-object),
[Response Object](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.1.html#response-object),
and [OpenAPI 3.0.4 Schema Object](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.0.4.html#schema-object).
MIT, matching the original public components.

# Timescale client and assigned-work receiving

This client uses the existing merchant MCP host, its original Timescale project, and its original retained-file receiver. It covers source editions, comparison review, refresh and job plans, publication, assigned remediation, complete reports and whole-project receiving. It adds no SQL endpoint, database, scheduler or server.

Configure the original host with [TIMESCALE_WORKSPACE.md](TIMESCALE_WORKSPACE.md). The installed command is `starforge timescale-client`. The programmatic export is `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/mcp/timescale/client`; its adjacent declaration file describes the original inputs and results.

## Start with the existing project

Use the MCP URL printed by the original `timescale-agent` or installed Applications start. Keep its bearer token in the agreed environment variable, outside request files and reports. The client accepts HTTPS, or the original loopback HTTP endpoint. It rejects URL credentials, fragments, query strings and redirects.

Work in an ordinary-user private directory:

```sh
umask 077
mkdir -p "$PWD/timescale-receiving"
cd "$PWD/timescale-receiving"

starforge timescale-client status \
  --url "$TIMESCALE_MCP_URL" --workspace usage \
  --workspace-id "$TIMESCALE_WORKSPACE_ID" \
  --token-env TIMESCALE_MCP_TOKEN
```

The persistent workspace ID comes from the existing host configuration/status. The client checks it on every reply. `open` first reads that declared identity, then opens or reuses the original publisher. It never silently opens a different project when an alias has changed.

The original browser and MCP tools share one model, journal, publisher and scheduler. Ending this client does not close that host. The explicit `close` method needs the actual current adapter and publisher instance IDs. Closing the borrowed resource keeps the original publisher owner until its normal owner close.

## Read exact sources and original results

Every method accepts the original JSON arguments through `--input PRIVATE_JSON`. Files must be private regular files under a private directory. `--input-sha256` optionally fixes their exact bytes. The command prints the returned original result as JSON.

| Method | Required selection |
| --- | --- |
| edition | editionId; optionally table, offset and limit |
| compare | beforeId, afterId; optionally offset and limit |
| plan | original planId |
| record | requestId and result/before; optionally native table and page |
| operation | action inspect/cancel and the original requestId |
| file | edition/result/before, original id, expectedSha256 and byte offset |
| remediation-sources | optional page of completed Remediate/Defer review choices |
| remediation-item | workItemId; select summary or an exact pinned history section |
| remediation-context | workItemId, itemRevision, itemDigest; optional later edition |

Native table cells remain exact strings or null. Decimal amounts, timestamps and PostgreSQL identifiers are not coerced into JavaScript numeric values. Complete source JSON and native result bytes remain available through the original file tools and full project export.

A comparison page is a view of the complete original comparison digest. A new review must account for every change, including later pages. The client does not generate approval or remediation decisions. A source choice exposes its original review, comparison, change and source digests plus changed field names. Full before/after values stay in the original editions and the complete work-item report; a shortened source summary is not substituted for those originals.

## Retain mutations before dispatch

Capture, review, refresh, verification, job changes, publication and work-item commands retain their existing request UUID. Prepare the complete request JSON before the call. The client does not generate a replacement UUID or replay a mutation when a response is lost.

```sh
starforge timescale-client remediation-command \
  --url "$TIMESCALE_MCP_URL" --workspace usage \
  --workspace-id "$TIMESCALE_WORKSPACE_ID" \
  --token-env TIMESCALE_MCP_TOKEN \
  --input "$PWD/assigned-work-request.json" \
  --input-sha256 "$REQUEST_FILE_SHA256" --wait-ms 600000
```

`--wait-ms` only reads that same accepted operation until it returns. A client interruption or observation timeout does not cancel or resubmit the server operation. Use `operation` with the same requestId to recover its actual result. `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` remains an unknown native outcome and requires the original reconciliation path.

If the original operation is FAILED or INTERRUPTED and its existing API permits continuation, inspect the cause and current workspace first. An explicit repeat uses the same request UUID and meaningful input; the current optimistic workspace version may be refreshed. A changed item, plan, source or requested action needs a reviewed new request. The server still verifies its original request digest.

## Assign and continue real work

The source must be a completed original comparison review with a Remediate or Defer decision. Creating work does not change that review. An item carries owner, due date, priority, intended work and acceptance condition.

The full source contract is in [the original remediation guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/postgres/timescale/REMEDIATION.md). All seven actions are available through the same merchant command:

| Action | Exact additional input |
| --- | --- |
| create | full source reference and work fields |
| edit | workItemId, expectedRevision and all mutable work fields |
| rebase | workItemId, expectedRevision and a later exact review of the same original catalog item |
| bind-plan | workItemId, expectedRevision, planId, planDigest and relevance |
| observe | workItemId, expectedRevision, original operationId/operationDigest and relevance |
| resolve | workItemId, expectedRevision and the full later-edition resolution |
| reopen | workItemId, expectedRevision and OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/DEFERRED |

Every command also needs requestId, expectedVersion, actor and note. Work fields contain title, owner, optional empty/actual YYYY-MM-DD dueDate, NORMAL/HIGH/URGENT priority, intent, acceptance and OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/DEFERRED status.

Use operation digests returned by the original remediation context. Do not hash a shortened MCP display and use that as the native operation digest. Observing an operation preserves its state at the recorded time; it does not rerun its refresh or job change.

CURRENT_STATE_REVIEW records the operator's assessment of a later retained catalog edition. It does not assert complete aggregate coverage. COMPLETE_AGGREGATE_VERIFICATION requires the original matching verification and exact plan/window, completed after the selected later edition. Earlier successful verification is not silently relabeled as coverage for a later source.

Read item summary first. To page `plans`, `observations` or `history`, send its exact itemRevision and itemDigest on every page. The response includes total and nextOffset. A changed item produces a conflict, so a receiver cannot join pages from different revisions. Full original operation bodies and source field values are also in the report JSON.

## Retain and receive the complete report

The report operation calls the original renderer. It stores its exact full JSON and printable HTML inside the original workspace at `remediation-reports/REQUEST_UUID`, with a manifest. The original exclusive writer records its request and completion. Existing whole-project export automatically includes that directory and the full earlier item history.

A report request is:

```json
{
  "requestId": "THE_NEW_REPORT_REQUEST_UUID",
  "expectedVersion": 42,
  "workItemId": "THE_ORIGINAL_WORK_ITEM_UUID",
  "itemRevision": 6,
  "itemDigest": "THE_EXACT_CURRENT_ITEM_SHA256"
}
```

Replace every shown value with the actual selected result. Run `remediation-report --input ... --wait-ms ...`, then `report-manifest` with `{"exportId":"THE_SAME_REPORT_UUID"}`. This manifest read performs no new rendering or database capture.

```sh
starforge timescale-client report-download \
  --url "$TIMESCALE_MCP_URL" --workspace usage \
  --workspace-id "$TIMESCALE_WORKSPACE_ID" \
  --token-env TIMESCALE_MCP_TOKEN \
  --export "$REPORT_REQUEST_ID" --directory "$PWD/received-report" \
  --expected-manifest-sha256 "$REPORT_MANIFEST_SHA256"
```

The directory receives the complete `Timescale_Remediation_Manifest.json`, `report.json` and `report.html`. Open the HTML directly. It uses the original script-free renderer and includes source decisions, linked plans, observed outcomes, resolution meaning and complete revision metadata.

Repeat the exact receiving command after interruption. The maintained receiver rechecks the original manifest, endpoint, workspace, file digests and retained byte prefix before continuing. A host restart can reopen the same completed report even after other project work has advanced. No source renderer is called for a completed report. If the MCP endpoint changes, its original endpoint binding must be restored or a new explicitly selected receiving directory used.

The report manifest is bounded at 64 KiB; each complete JSON/HTML file is bounded at 256 MiB. Oversized reports fail clearly before final publication. The full original workspace package remains available. Reads use the existing immutable file descriptors and at most196,608 bytes per chunk; the whole report is not copied into memory for each chunk.

## Programmatic workflow

```js
import { openTimescaleClient } from
  '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/mcp/timescale/client';

const client = await openTimescaleClient({
  url: process.env.TIMESCALE_MCP_URL,
  workspace: 'usage',
  workspaceId: process.env.TIMESCALE_WORKSPACE_ID,
  tokenEnv: 'TIMESCALE_MCP_TOKEN'
});
await client.open();
const status = await client.status();
const choices = await client.remediation.sources({offset: 0, limit: 25});

// Load this complete original request from the caller's retained private file.
// The source/plan/item references come from the actual inspected choices.
const accepted = await client.remediation.command(savedRequest);
const operation = await client.wait(accepted.id);
if (operation.state !== 'COMPLETE') {
  throw new Error('Inspect the original operation: ' + operation.id);
}

const selected = await client.remediation.item({
  workItemId: operation.result.workItemId
});
const page = await client.remediation.item({
  workItemId: selected.item.id,
  itemRevision: selected.item.revision,
  itemDigest: selected.itemDigest,
  section: 'history', offset: 0, limit: 25
});
// Follow page.page.nextOffset with the same item pin for every remaining row.

const originalReport = await client.remediation.inspectReport({
  exportId: savedReportRequest.requestId
});
await client.remediation.downloadReport({
  exportId: savedReportRequest.requestId,
  directory: process.env.TIMESCALE_REPORT_DIRECTORY,
  expectedManifestSha256: originalReport.manifestSha256
});
```

The client exposes typed original capture, edition, comparison, review, refresh, verify, job, publication, operation, plan, record, file and browser methods alongside remediation. It also exposes `exports.inspect` and `exports.download` for the existing whole-project format. Raw `call` is restricted to the declared Timescale methods, with the same persistent scope.

## Full project handover and reopening

Create a new original workspace export after report retention. Receive it with `timescale-client download` or `client.exports.download`. The maintained native package includes the Timescale journal, all source editions/results, publisher state, original dataset generations, empty directories and every retained remediation report. Existing source configuration and environment-reference rules are preserved.

# Approved order to paid file

The original receiver can now participate in a complete merchant purchase. An
operator enrolls an actual private file and creates its order handoff. The buyer
adds that order to the existing SF88 operation, reviews the exact URL and payment
terms, and uses the existing approval and spending workflow. The original SF30
seller runs the order application through its Python worker pool; native
settlement writes the original SF98 event. Its authenticated delivery unlocks the
file in the same SF101 database. The customer downloads the exact promised bytes.

The merchant's private file, enrolled order, token hash and entitlement stay in
the existing `receiver.py` store. The checkout does not introduce another order
database, payment engine, approval provider or signer. Each checkout listener
offers one fixed-price GET operation with one complete Stellar payment option.
Multiple approved files/orders can use that operation. Deploy separate original
merchant configurations when product prices or payment options differ.

## The order is part of the approved resource

The request has both:

```text
GET https://merchant.example/purchase/report?sf98_order=approved-order-482
X-SF98-Order-ID: approved-order-482
```

The new optional SF88 `operation.orderReference` derives this one header and
requires the same single `sf98_order` query value. The original SF31 approval
intent already includes the complete URL, and the existing SF54 mapper includes
that URL in the exact SF36 consent request. No financial schema change is needed.
The same normalized operation survives original SF88 queue storage and restart.

Before payment processing, the merchant requires the query and header to match,
looks up the original approved order, checks its route, method, network, amount,
asset and available recipient binding, and reads the original enrolled file to
confirm its size and hash. Unknown, changed or already entitled orders do not
reach native payment processing. The application repeats the original order/file
read after verification; application failure takes SF30's existing cancellation
path before settlement.

When the original receiver supplies its `access_allowed(db, ref)` policy helper,
the same read checks it before verification and again in the application. Order
and policy reads share one explicit SQLite read transaction. A
suspended or expired pending order cannot enter checkout. Older receiver source
without that optional helper retains its original access behavior; checkout does
not create a second policy store.

The order reference is a constrained, nonsecret identifier. It will appear in the
approved URL and normal merchant request records. It is not the claim token. The
claim token is provisioned separately, never placed in the URL, handoff, x402
payload, outbox event or buyer file receipt.

## Merchant setup

Use Node 22.16 or newer, Python 3.11 or newer and the existing repository source.
Native settlement uses the original installed `@x402/core`, `@x402/stellar` and
`@x402/extensions` packages. Version 2.28.0 was used for the focused local journey.
The operator owns the existing HTTPS reverse proxy and native facilitator.

Put this configuration in a private file outside the source checkout. Replace
the resource description, origin, paths and payment terms with the merchant's
actual approved values. The two `UNVERIFIED_DEMO_*` markers compile for local
inspection but are not usable payment details.

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.sf101.checkout-service.v1",
  "publicOrigin": "https://merchant.example",
  "path": "/purchase/report",
  "routeId": "paid_report",
  "description": "Purchase the previously approved private report",
  "payment": {
    "scheme": "exact",
    "network": "stellar:testnet",
    "amount": "1000",

```

From the repository root:

```sh

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf101-merchant-receiver/checkout.mjs init \

```

Inspection reads configuration and original offer schemas. Initialization calls

### Enroll the actual file

Use the merchant's existing secure mechanism to generate and provision a long
random claim token. Place it in `SF101_CLAIM_TOKEN` for enrollment. The buyer
receives that same token through the separately authorized private channel.
Use an opaque printable token of 32–1024 bytes without whitespace; a randomly
generated 64-character hexadecimal token is suitable for this interface.

The file must be a private regular file, 1 byte to 32 MiB, with no group or other
access. `receiver.py` reads and hashes the actual bytes during enrollment.

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf101-merchant-receiver/checkout.mjs enroll \
  --config /private/merchant/checkout.json \
  --ref approved-order-482 \
  --file /private/merchant/reports/report-482.csv \
  --out /private/merchant/handoffs/order-482.json
```

Use `--claim-env NAME` when the existing private environment uses another name.
Only that selected value is passed to the original enrollment process. The
persistent Python checkout workers receive neither the token nor the webhook
HMAC key.

Enrollment derives route/method/price and asset/recipient digests from the same
compiled seller offer, then calls original `receiver.enroll()`. The emitted
handoff is create-only, 0600 JSON with the order, purchase and delivery URLs,
accepted payment terms, and promised file hash/size. It contains no file path or
token. Supply this exact handoff to the customer through the existing merchant
relationship.

If enrollment completed but the handoff could not be saved, recover that same
order without enrolling or rotating its token again:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf101-merchant-receiver/checkout.mjs handoff \
  --config /private/merchant/checkout.json \
  --ref approved-order-482 \
  --out /private/merchant/handoffs/recovered-order-482.json
```

Existing orders without the receiver's optional recipient digest are labeled
`ORIGINAL_LEGACY_ORDER` in the handoff. A receiver with recipient binding stores
and checks the supplied digest and produces `ORIGINAL_RECIPIENT_DIGEST`. The
checkout never silently rewrites or upgrades a legacy order.

## Original notification and customer download

The merchant delivers the original SF98 outbox using its existing worker or
explicit drain command. The HMAC key must match the original receiver.

```sh

  --state /private/merchant/sf98-outbox \
  --url https://merchant.example/internal/x402-events \
```

An accepted original notification changes the enrolled order to `ENTITLED` in

On the buyer's machine, put the separately provisioned token in the private
`SF101_CLAIM_TOKEN` environment value, then run:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf101-merchant-receiver/purchase.mjs retrieve \
  --handoff /private/buyer/order-482.json \
  --out /private/buyer/downloads/report-482.csv
```

This sends one GET to the handoff's exact same-merchant `/deliver/<order>` path,
with its token in `Authorization`. It uses the original public HTTPS transport's
DNS pinning, TLS checks, no redirects and body deadline. It has no payment
fallback. A 404 for a pending order or rejected token creates no final file;
repair the merchant notification/token and explicitly retrieve again.

On Linux the same command retains and resumes an interrupted download. The buyer
checks its saved prefix, requests the missing range from the original receiver,
and feeds the prefix and exact returned suffix through the original response-file
writer. Complete size and SHA-256 verification precede its create-only final path.
The new file, private transfer state and adjacent `.sf101.json` receipt use 0600
permissions. The [resumable transfer guide](RESUMABLE_TRANSFERS.md) covers status,
restart, graceful cancellation, process recovery and proxy configuration.

Rerunning `retrieve` when the final file already exists checks its actual private
bytes first. Matching bytes reuse or repair the local file receipt without a
network request or token. A different, non-private or symlinked file is refused
without replacement. Local possession of a previously downloaded copy is not a
new access grant; server-side suspension cannot retract an existing local copy.

Keep the original buyer financial outcome, original merchant entitlement receipt
and local downloaded-file receipt together in the merchant's existing workflow.
The last records completed local bytes, not independently verified Stellar
settlement or cash collection. The original receiver receipt remains available:

```sh
python3 stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf101-merchant-receiver/receiver.py receipt \
  --state /private/merchant/sf101 --ref approved-order-482 \
  --out /private/merchant/receipts/order-482.json
```

## Operational behavior and validation

Prepayment reads and the post-verification read use the original bounded Python
pool. An application failure withholds the purchase response and lets the native
seller cancel before settlement. Original SF98 journal failure after successful
native settlement remains a merchant reconciliation event; checkout logs
`SF101_NATIVE_OUTBOX_WRITE_FAILED` and does not pretend it can undo settlement.
Concurrent independently approved purchases are separate attempts. There is no
one-charge guarantee across different intents or a crash before notification.

The focused `checkout.journey.mjs` runs actual local Python/SQLite, original SF88
configuration/inbox/review, SF31 resource approval and SF54 mapping, official
x402 2.28.0 SF30 processing, original SF98 HMAC HTTP sender, original SF101
receiver, and original streamed file writer. It covers pending/wrong-token
denial, mismatched order rejection before verification, exact delivered bytes,
receiver restart, duplicate event acknowledgement, local-file recovery and
wrong-hash withholding. Its facilitator and approval are controlled locally;
the check does not submit a transaction or claim a live customer payment.

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf101-merchant-receiver/checkout.journey.mjs
```

Source ownership stays with the original SF30/Python, SF88 onramp, SF98 sender,
SF101 receiver/access and SF10 grant teams. This is delivered product integration
for the existing merchant pilot and canonical grant application.

# Receive the original ETIM supplier delivery through the material MCP

This program takes the complete published ETIM supplier example through the maintained material and supplier tools. It begins with the original supplier delivery operation, keeps its catalog, review and correction identities, adds the publisher's unit, classification and GTIN fields to the catalog mapping, and delivers the updated workspace to a second customer workspace. The typed client, command line client, retained downloads and merchant host all use the original catalog, supplier and request stores.

The same command is a continuation after an interruption. Its private operation directory retains the original request IDs, input hashes, export manifests, file checkpoints and customer revisions. Keep that directory together with the original supplier directory.

## Run the complete receiving operation

Use the current complete product source, Node 24 with the original SQLite support, Python and the original supplier program's XML validation dependencies. The source tree must include the maintained merchant operator, seller SDK and the four original ETIM source files. The ordinary supplier delivery program performs its original source and official schema validation before this continuation begins.

From the repository root:

~~~sh
node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/receiving/opensearch-materials-native.mjs \
  --supplier-directory /private/receiving/supplier-etim \
  --directory /private/receiving/materials-mcp \
  --supplier-operation supplier-etim-2769 \
  --operation opensearch-materials-2769
~~~

The two directories must be separate canonical paths owned by the current operator. Their permissions must exclude other users. The program creates its own new directories with mode 0700. It does not accept a symlink in place of either selected directory or overlapping directories.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| --supplier-directory | Original supplier operation directory. An existing completed operation is reopened and its retained artifacts are verified. |
| --directory | Private material MCP receiving directory containing the control state, host configuration, customer workspace and downloads. |
| --supplier-operation | Original supplier operation ID; defaults to supplier-etim-2769. Preserve it on continuation. |

| --help | Print the command and continuation requirements. |

The JavaScript entry point is exported for a maintained native receiving runner:

## Complete operating flow

The control report records the following complete phases under their stable names.

| Phase | Result retained by the original operation |
| --- | --- |
| original_receiver | Reopen the original supplier receiver; compare its catalog, selected edition, plan, correction, review, product and source identities. |
| original_match_and_query | Save a customer approval for the published description and create an ordinary merchant query draft from the selected catalog. |
| original_unit_and_classification | Stream the exact declared source, save the enriched mapping, review and select its edition, inspect changed fields, page real facets and convert 5.25 C62 to the exact rational value 21/4. |
| reviewed_supplier_and_customer_selection | Move the original supplier plan to the reviewed edition, clear the redundant earlier correction against exact revision and product pins, retain all original fields, review the product and renew the customer's original match. |
| complete_original_exports | Produce all ten material and four supplier formats through the original retained export operations, inspect their manifests and explicitly open and release a manifest file read. |
| interrupted_original_download | Receive a verified non-final portion of the actual portable bundle, record the original durable checkpoint, then interrupt and close the host. |
| resumed_complete_original_files | Restart the original host, continue the same verified prefix, finish every file and repeat the complete download to verify its retained contents. |
| complete_customer_receiving | Import the complete downloaded bundle into the second original workspace through its host-declared input alias; retain the original catalog, supplier and decision identities. |

## The actual interruption and continuation

The interruption is placed inside the original downloader's onProgress callback after it has saved a verified, non-final prefix of catalog-bundle.jsonl. It is not simulated by editing download state or replacing an exported file. The program records the actual export ID, filename, byte offset and total, throws its own receiving interruption, and closes the maintained host.

The following phase starts the same original host and calls the same download operation, directory and expected manifest SHA-256. Completion requires the downloader to report a resumed verified prefix. The finished download is repeated and every retained output is opened and hashed again.

Request bodies are written into control state before a mutation is sent. Exact retries use the original request body and request ID. Completed native operations are matched by their original operation identity and request digest. The program retains the current business state after a historical retry so that later customer work remains visible.

| Interruption boundary | Same-operation continuation |
| --- | --- |
| Before a mutation returns | Reuse its saved exact request and read the original returned operation. |
| After an export is sealed | Reopen its retained manifest and original complete files. |
| During an export before sealing | The maintained export adapter can recover its private unsealed operation while the explicit original selection still matches. |
| After a verified download prefix | Resume the original endpoint, workspace alias, export ID, manifest and directory. |
| After complete download but before phase state is saved | The original downloader verifies and adopts the exact existing files. |
| After customer import but before its response is retained | Replay the original receive request against the same customer workspace. |
| After newer customer work | Historical receive and correction requests preserve the original newer revisions. |
| After a completed phase | Reuse its saved result, then reconcile every final manifest and local artifact before returning completion. |
| After a control-state storage failure | Stop further effects and keep the same operation directory for the next continuation. |

If the selected port is still occupied, first reconcile the original host process associated with the retained operation. Starting another receiving directory or choosing a different request identity does not continue an existing file checkpoint.

If an exported file has been removed or changed, the program refuses to return its previous successful metadata as a new completion. It opens the actual retained regular file, streams its current contents, checks the original length and SHA-256, and compares file identity before and after the read. The same checks run when all earlier phases were already complete.

# Native facilitator operator

Use the original native facilitator from a local operator screen: review a profile, retain its original JSON file, start the SDK backend, inspect its accounts and payment state, drain it, and reopen the same configuration. The browser and original CLI use the same configuration schema and runtime.

## Start the workspace

Choose a private workspace and the **same shared signer ownership directory used by the other native facilitator processes on this host**. Keep those paths canonical and absolute. Use the existing configured Stellar accounts and secret environment-variable names. Set the actual secrets in the host environment before launching.

```sh
node native-facilitator/workspace/server.mjs \
  --directory /private/facilitator-operator \
  --ownership-directory /private/stellar-signer-ownership \
  --create --port 0
```

`--create` creates those private leaf directories when their parents already exist. On later starts the same paths reopen the saved profiles. Open the complete local URL printed by the command. The URL grants access to this local operator; keep it in the operator session. A new workspace process prints a new URL.

## Review and retain a profile

Enter the network, selected RPC, existing public settlement accounts and their environment-variable references, allowed asset contracts and recipients, maximum atomic amount, fee ceiling and account capacity. Select the accepted native payment timing. Authorization completes merchant work before settlement; upfront settles before opening the merchant source. The merchant's advertised timing must match the facilitator profile.

The review calls the original `validateConfig` and `reviewConfig` without loading signing material. It shows the complete recipient, asset, amount, timing, fees, account references and configuration digest. Capacity is limited by the distinct configured accounts. A readiness probe uses the original RPC readiness implementation.

Save under a unique profile name. The resulting `profiles/<name>.json` is the original normalized native configuration, written privately and published only after its complete bytes have been synced. Saving the same name and exact review again reopens that profile. A different configuration needs a new name. Importing or editing an existing profile preserves its shared ownership directory; a profile naming another directory requires launching the workspace with that original host directory.

The file can be supplied directly to the original `native-facilitator/cli.mjs --review|--serve --config FILE`, or selected as the native facilitator configuration in the original SF66 merchant/customer setup. The selected-profile panel supplies the exact file path, native download and original CLI argument arrays. A changed file must be reviewed again before it can start.

## Run and observe

Select a saved profile, choose the local HTTP listener port, and start its backend. Port zero assigns a free port. Startup loads the existing environment references and uses `createNativeFacilitator` plus `startFacilitatorServer`. The existing SDK owns payment verification, signing, fee sponsorship and settlement. The original shared ownership lease protects its configured accounts. No backend starts automatically when the operator page or process reopens.

The running panel shows its exact profile digest and runtime identity, network and payment timings, original supported metadata, each settlement account's state, active work, available capacity, native verification/settlement counts, refusals and errors. Counters describe the current runtime. The buyer and merchant retain their own purchase receipts and outputs through their original workflows. Configure any deployment gateway against the displayed listener using the existing native facilitator operating guide.

The operator screen is authenticated separately from the native facilitator HTTP endpoint. Both bind to loopback. The management API verifies the exact local origin and its printed session capability. Key values are never requested by the form or returned by the runtime status.

## Drain, update and reopen

Use **Drain and stop** before choosing another profile or port. The original transport stops admitting requests and drains the original SDK. The operator process also retains those descriptors during shutdown. Review the original merchant/buyer operation before retrying any payment after a lost connection.

The fulfillment page then provides this complete operator path:

Incident filtering covers active, recovered or all retained records, with stable

## Composition API

`startSellerOperations(session, {deliveryOutbox, deliveryControls:true, deliveryRecovery})` returns `deliveryControlUrl` along with its original listener, observer and close function. The optional recovery callback receives `{id, expectedRevision}` and must operate on the same original outbox. `startCheckout` forwards this callback.

For the complete same-listener application, pass `deliveryWorkspaceDirectory`
and optional `incidentSource:{directory,merchantId}` instead of an injected
`deliveryRecovery`. The launcher opens the existing `openDeliveryWorkspace` model
against `deliveryOutbox.dir`, mounts its existing handler, and returns
`deliveryWorkspace` and `deliveryWorkspaceUrl`. `deliveryWorkspaceOptions` forwards
the original trusted delivery options for native integration. Closing operations
also closes its owned workspace model and releases its original supervisor lease.
`startCheckout` forwards these options. The merchant launcher's `--check` validates
the directory/registration option syntax without opening either state directory.

The shared `sf98-merchant-delivery/delivery-recovery.mjs` exports:

- `deliveryRevision(row)`: SHA-256 of the original event ID and exact native state.
- `inspectDelivery(outbox, id)`: original row and current revision.
- `requeueDelivery(outbox, {id, expectedRevision, lease?})`: rechecks the exact original EXHAUSTED state and invokes the original outbox requeue. A supplied original lease is validated against the same outbox; otherwise the helper acquires and releases it. This lets existing receiver-workspace batch maintenance compose the helper without nested lease acquisition.

The listener uses its existing loopback Host/origin policy and an additional per-process capability for recovery. POST `/api/delivery/requeue` requires the exact same-origin `Origin`, `x-delivery-control`, and a JSON object with only `id` and `expectedRevision`. Successful recovery returns the original event/revision transition; stale revisions receive409. The browser never receives receiver secrets, wallet material or payment headers.

GET `/api/delivery/events` accepts `state` (attention/all/native state), `routeId`, `cursor` (last original event ID) and `limit` (1–100). The cursor follows original append order even when a previously displayed event changes state. GET `/api/delivery/event?id=...` returns the selected event and revision; `/api/delivery/control` reports availability without the capability value.

GET `/api/delivery/incidents` accepts `state` (active/all/recovered), `cursor`
(original incident UUID) and `limit` (1–100). GET `/api/delivery/incident?id=...`
returns the selected registered merchant incident. POST
`/api/delivery/incident/ack` uses the same private capability/origin requirements
and accepts exactly `{id,expectedRevision,by,notes}`. Its revision is the original
incident's integer revision; delivery requeue retains its separate SHA-256 state
revision. The original SF93 transaction performs the acknowledgment and its
configured notification behavior.

# Finite SSE and NDJSON purchases

Use the original buyer request and response-file writer to consume a finite event
stream. The writer saves the exact response bytes while the shared parser delivers
complete records. A successful save has the same `path`, `bytes`, `sha256`,
`contentType` and `cleanupWarnings` fields as an ordinary saved response, plus a
`stream` summary. The original payment result and accounting continuation remain
attached to the same request.

## Select the payment flow explicitly

An omitted `expect.paymentFlow` selects `authorization`. Use
`expect.paymentFlow: 'upfront'` only for the matching offered requirement when
settlement before generation is the intended purchase. The native signer compares
that selection, its independent operator configuration, and the complete original
accepted terms. The merchant's response format alone cannot select the payment flow.

For an authorization stream, the original seller finishes generation before native
settlement and transfer. For an upfront stream, the native supported flow settles
before live generation. The buyer always makes its original unsigned request and
at most one signed request. Event IDs and `retry` fields never cause a reconnect.

## Capture and consume the same bytes

Prepare output before invoking the buyer. `client`, `approve`, `sign`, and `expect`
below are the application's existing native buyer, approval, signer and selected
merchant terms. `destination` is a new absolute filename in a trusted directory.

```js
import { prepareBuyerResponseFile } from './response-file.mjs';

const output = await prepareBuyerResponseFile({
  destination,
  maxBytes: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
  timeoutMs: 120000,
  stream: { format: 'sse', maxRecordBytes: 1024 * 1024, maxRecords: 100000 },
});

try {
  const result = await client.call({
    url, method: 'POST', body, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
    expect, approve, sign, intentId, signal,
  });
  const saved = await output.save(result, {
    signal,
    async onRecord(record) {
      // Called after the corresponding raw bytes have been written.
      // Awaiting this callback provides application backpressure.
      await renderProgress(record.event, record.data, record.id);
    },
  });
  await retainPurchase({ result, saved });
} finally {
  await output.abort();
}
```

For NDJSON use `format: 'ndjson'`. Its callback receives
`{ index, format: 'ndjson', value }`. SSE callbacks receive
`{ index, format: 'sse', event, data, id, retry? }`. Indices start at zero. `retry`
retains a valid server instruction as metadata; this capture never acts on it.
The callback is optional. Its failure or stalled promise is governed by the same
capture deadline, cancellation and partial-file handling as the original response.
Progress callbacks precede the final file hash and completion checks; retain the
successful save receipt before treating a whole response as complete.
An arriving chunk can contain several complete records. Cancellation from one
callback retains all bytes already written, so reopening may expose additional
complete records from that same chunk. Use the recorded indices when continuing
application processing.

## Use the original native operator

The same options are accepted in `operator.json`:

```json
{
  "responseFile": {
    "destination": "/absolute/private/operator/events.sse",
    "maxBytes": 67108864,
    "timeoutMs": 120000,
    "stream": { "format": "sse", "maxRecordBytes": 1048576, "maxRecords": 100000 }
  }
}
```

Merge this field into the existing complete operator configuration and keep
`captureBody` absent or `false`. The original review prints the selected output
configuration. The original execute path starts capture as soon as the buyer
returns the response, while its existing accounting observation continues. Native
streaming transport uses the selected capture duration when `requestTimeoutMs`
is omitted, with a maximum of 300000 ms. A top-level `requestTimeoutMs` selects
the complete HTTP exchange deadline explicitly, including DNS, TLS, response
headers and body consumption. `responseFile.timeoutMs` starts when capture begins.
Each limit is independent, and the first one reached ends the transfer.

The private result is still `responseFile.status: 'SAVED'` on complete delivery.
Its additional summary includes `format`, `records`, parsed `bytes`, `complete`,
`pendingRecord`, and `lastCompleteByte`; SSE also carries `lastEventId` and the
last valid `retryMilliseconds`. Stream options are local capture limits and do not
change the accepted price or spending reservation.

The maintained [Node application reader](../sf88-operator-buyer-cli/node/STREAMS.md)
opens these same retained bytes through `events()` and `ndjson()`.

## Framing and completion

| Property | SSE | NDJSON |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Media type | `text/event-stream` | `application/x-ndjson` or `application/ndjson` |
| Encoding | UTF-8; invalid bytes fail | UTF-8; invalid bytes fail |
| Record delimiter | Blank line; LF, CRLF and lone CR accepted | LF; an immediately preceding CR is accepted |
| Data | Consecutive `data` fields join with LF | One JSON value per nonempty line |
| Metadata | Standard `event`, persistent `id`, numeric `retry`; comments and unknown fields ignored | Empty and whitespace-only lines ignored |
| End of body | An unfinished event stays undispatched | A final JSON value without LF stays undispatched |

One initial UTF-8 BOM is removed. SSE fields split at their first colon, and only
one optional leading space is removed from the field value. A NUL in an `id`
field causes that field to be ignored. `[DONE]` has no special parser meaning; an
application may interpret it as ordinary event data.
An explicit charset must be UTF-8/utf8 and occur at most once in the content type.

`maxRecordBytes` bounds wire bytes in one pending framed record. `maxRecords`
bounds dispatched records. The separate original `maxBytes` limit bounds the
whole saved response. A body ending with an unfinished event or NDJSON line
returns `RESPONSE_STREAM_INCOMPLETE_RECORD` and retains the partial capture.
Normal connection closure completes only the HTTP capture; any application-level
end marker belongs to that application's own contract.

The framing follows [WHATWG's event-stream parsing rules](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream)
and the [NDJSON serialization/parsing specification](https://github.com/ndjson/ndjson-spec#3-functional-specification).
This finite acquisition applies fatal UTF-8 validation and an explicit incomplete
tail result in addition to the standard field dispatch rules.

## Continue after an interruption

On a stopped, failed, malformed or over-limit stream, the existing response-file
error still contains its original `bytes`, `partialPath` and `cleanupWarnings`.
Streaming adds `partialSha256`, the digest of exactly those written bytes, and
`stream.lastCompleteByte`, the end of the last complete frame. The original SF88
summary retains these fields alongside its existing payment and accounting result.
The final destination is published only after complete capture and its configured
integrity checks succeed.

Node's explicit `events({ allowPartial: true })` and
`ndjson({ allowPartial: true })` inspect the recorded complete prefix after
verifying the retained partial-file hash. They reopen the same operation and do
not start a request. Use the existing native financial continuation for the
original payment outcome and the merchant's own recovery procedure for additional
delivery; reopening the local stream does not change either operation.

The pure shared parser exports `createResponseStreamParser(options)` with
`push(Uint8Array)`, `finish()` and `summary()` for hosts already consuming raw
bytes. `parseResponseStream(asyncIterable, options)` provides a backpressured
async iterator with the same strict completion result.

```sh
  --processing-workspace /private/processing \
  --processing-config /private/processing-config.json \
  > /private/stac-host.json
```

Omit the two processing flags for imagery alone. The original host remains
running in its terminal. The clients bind to the original loopback address and
workspace ID; they do not start, stop or replace this process.

In another terminal, create the client connection:

```sh
starforge stac-workspace connection-init \
  --out /private/stac-connection.json \
  --console-url-file /private/stac-host.json \
  --workspace imagery

starforge stac-workspace status --connection /private/stac-connection.json
```

The output file must be new and its parent directory must already be private
(mode 0700). Connection files and original startup records require mode 0600
and the current host user. Use `--workspace-id` when the selected private file
contains a plain native URL rather than its complete JSON startup record.

A complete connection can contain several independently owned hosts:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.stac-workspace-connection.v1",
  "workspaces": {
    "imagery": {
      "label": "Current imagery review",
      "consoleUrlFile": "./stac-host.json",
      "timeoutMs": 60000,
      "maxResponseBytes": 134217728,
      "inputs": {
        "received-scenes": {
          "path": "./incoming/stac-workspace-handover.json",
          "kind": "imagery-handover"
        },
        "received-processing": {
          "path": "./incoming/processing-handover.json",
          "kind": "processing-handover"
        }
      },
      "processingProfiles": {}
    }
  }
}
```

Relative host paths resolve beside the connection JSON. An input can also pin
its original `sha256`. The permitted input kinds are `imagery-handover`,
`processing-handover`, `processing-source` and `processing-page`.

A host can select `consoleUrlEnv` instead of `consoleUrlFile`. That names one
host environment variable containing the original JSON startup record or URL.
A plain URL also requires the expected `workspaceId`. Agent tool arguments
never contain the private URL, cookie, CSRF token, credential variable value or
input filesystem path.

After the original host restarts, replace its private startup file with the new
native record. The next client request rereads that file, establishes the new
session and verifies the same saved workspace ID. A different workspace is a
specific identity error before a workspace action is dispatched.

## Review and acquire imagery

Start from `status`, which returns the original revision, saved collection
counts and enabled processing capabilities.

```sh
starforge stac-workspace records --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --kind collections --offset 0 --limit 50

starforge stac-workspace records --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --kind editions --offset 0 --limit 50
```

For another page, pass the returned `nextOffset` and original `revision`.
A changed revision asks you to restart that view, so concurrent edits cannot
silently shift records between pages. Continue until `nextOffset` is null.
Complete JSON is also available through `download --kind state`.

If catalog discovery is needed, use the original operation with the current
revision:

```sh
starforge stac-workspace discover --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --operation-id analyst-catalog-20261012 --revision CURRENT_REVISION \
  --wait-ms 60000
```

Prepare a native query JSON file. The following is a spatial/date selection;
the original discovered catalog determines whether its collection and query
extension are available.

```json
{
  "name": "Austin September review",
  "collections": ["sentinel-2-l2a"],
  "bbox": [-98.0, 30.0, -97.5, 30.5],
  "datetime": "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z/2026-09-30T23:59:59Z",
  "cloudCoverMax": 20,
  "pageSize": 100,
  "maxPages": 20
}
```

Exactly one of `bbox` and GeoJSON `intersects` is required. The native query
validator keeps STAC coordinate/date rules, including antimeridian bounds.
`maxPages` is the original acquisition budget. To update a saved query, include
its existing `id`; an existing saved review remains bound to the earlier exact
query values and catalog sources.

```sh
starforge stac-workspace query-save --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --query-file /private/query.json --revision CURRENT_REVISION

starforge stac-workspace search-review --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --query-id SAVED_QUERY_ID
```

Read the returned review, including the original request, query digest,
collection contracts and page budget. Then choose the original acquisition:

```sh
starforge stac-workspace search-acquire --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --review-id SAVED_REVIEW_ID --operation-id analyst-capture-20261012 \
  --wait-ms 60000

starforge stac-workspace operation --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --operation-id analyst-capture-20261012
```

The host returns a recent job while the original workspace records the saved
edition and native page progress. Native operations retain their source
identities and outcomes. Inspect the same ID after a connection failure.
No client method automatically retries a mutation.

A client wait timeout or interruption stops waiting; it does not cancel the
original provider operation. Use `search-cancel --edition-id ID` to request
native cancellation. Use `search-resume --edition-id ID --operation-id ID`
for the explicit original continuation. A resume keeps the same edition and
captured pages. After a host restart, its recent in-memory job list can be empty;
`operation` also reads the durable original workspace operation record.

## Inspect scenes, comparisons, decisions and assets

`edition` returns the native edition, coverage and a digest of its complete
item/decision/asset view. `items` returns full original STAC features, not reduced
geometry or rewritten source attributes:

```sh
starforge stac-workspace edition --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --edition-id SAVED_EDITION_ID

starforge stac-workspace items --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --edition-id SAVED_EDITION_ID --offset 0 --limit 25

starforge stac-workspace item --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --edition-id SAVED_EDITION_ID --item-id COLLECTION_QUALIFIED_ITEM_ID
```

Continue item pages with the returned `viewSha256` as `--view-sha`.
An active edition adding pages or changed analyst metadata produces a changed
view digest. Item IDs use the original percent-encoded collection and item ID,
joined by `/`; use the exact `itemId` returned by the client.

Compare two retained editions through the original comparison engine:

```sh
starforge stac-workspace compare --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --left-edition-id BASELINE_ID --right-edition-id CURRENT_ID \
  --kind changed --offset 0 --limit 25
```

The result preserves both coverage descriptions, `comparableQuery`, counts for
all four categories, and the original added/removed/changed/unchanged rows.
Page each category with the same view digest. Download the complete comparison
JSON when passing the analysis to another application.

A decision file contains `editionId`, `itemId`, `status`, `actor`,
`note`, `assetKeys` and the current `expectedRevision`. Status is one of
`SELECTED`, `REJECTED` or `REVIEW`. Native validation keeps the item and
selected asset keys attached to the same edition.

```sh
starforge stac-workspace decision-save --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --args-file /private/decision.json

starforge stac-workspace asset-review --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --edition-id SAVED_EDITION_ID --item-id COLLECTION_QUALIFIED_ITEM_ID \
  --asset-key thumbnail --max-bytes 1048576

starforge stac-workspace asset-acquire --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --review-id SAVED_ASSET_REVIEW_ID --operation-id analyst-thumbnail-20261012 \
  --wait-ms 60000

starforge stac-workspace download --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --kind asset --asset-id SAVED_ASSET_ID --out /private/received-thumbnail.jpg
```

The original provider controls asset eligibility and the reviewed maximum
bytes. Asset downloads stream to a private temporary file and hash the complete
body before publication, so native assets up to 2 GiB do not require a whole-file
memory buffer. Set the host connection timeout to cover the expected transfer. Completed asset downloads verify original byte length and SHA256.
The client publishes a complete file atomically without replacing an existing
file. A final directory-sync error includes the published filename and digest;
read that actual destination before choosing a continuation.

## Cirrus processing on the same workspace

Processing status comes from the original configured controller. Its capability
list declares the enabled read/action names; unavailable capabilities are
specific native errors.

```sh
starforge stac-workspace processing-status \
  --connection /private/stac-connection.json

starforge stac-workspace processing-read --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --name runs --query-file /private/processing-edition-query.json \
  --path runs --offset 0 --limit 25
```

Here `processing-edition-query.json` contains the native `editionId`.
Other original reads include `inventory`, `statistics`, `edition`,
`run` and `associations`. Use the original read's required query fields.
For a large nested array, `--path` selects its own-property path; successive
pages use the returned view digest. Full processing views can be downloaded
as JSON.

Use `processing-action` for the original `discover`, `prepare-inventory`,
`review`, `prepare-capture`, `capture`, `resume`, `cancel`,
`prepare-continuation`, `continue-page`, `associate` and
`export-handover` actions supported by that host. The input JSON uses the
original controller contract. Saved review IDs, edition IDs, task IDs and
expected capture digests pass through unchanged.

```sh
starforge stac-workspace processing-action --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --name export-handover --input-file /private/processing-export.json \
  --operation-id analyst-processing-export-20261012 --wait-ms 60000

starforge stac-workspace download --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --kind processing-handover --export-id analyst-processing-export-20261012 \
  --out /private/processing-handover.json
```

The export input contains the native `editionIds` and
`includeStacAssets` selection. Processing handover bytes, filename, manifest,
byte count and SHA256 come from the original portable exporter.

Host configuration and full source files have explicit input aliases.
A `processingProfiles` entry contains the unchanged native `deployment`,
a declared `processing-source` `sourceInput`, optional `sourceMetadata`
and a label. The host user supplies those values, including any original auth
environment-variable selection. Agents choose the profile alias, reviewed
source SHA256, current processing revision and stable operation ID:

```sh
starforge stac-workspace processing-configure --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --profile DEPLOYMENT_ALIAS --sha256 SOURCE_SHA256 --revision CURRENT_REVISION \
  --operation-id analyst-processing-config-20261012
```

Provider-specific session/S3 adapters stay with the original host. This client
does not interpret their credentials or replace their SDK.

## Complete handover, import and reopen

Download the original imagery handover with its complete captured source files,
editions, item review inputs, decisions and optional saved assets:

```sh
starforge stac-workspace download --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --kind handover --edition-ids BASELINE_ID,CURRENT_ID --include-assets true \
  --out /private/stac-workspace-handover.json
```

Create a receiving workspace through the original `stac` commands, run its
original host, and add that host as another alias. Declare the received handover
as an input, inspect it, and import the exact reviewed bytes:

```sh
starforge stac-workspace input-inspect --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --workspace received --input received-scenes

starforge stac-workspace input-import --connection /private/stac-connection.json \
  --workspace received --input received-scenes --sha256 REVIEWED_SHA256
```

The native imagery importer verifies its canonical handover digest, every file's
size and SHA256, endpoint compatibility and saved record identities. Reimporting
the same exact handover returns its original import receipt. A conflicting saved
edition or file remains a native conflict.

Processing handover imports additionally require `--operation-id`.
A declared `processing-page` input requires its existing `--edition-id`,
`--task-id` and original metadata JSON; the native importer determines whether
that page can complete the retained task. These operations use the complete
original bytes rather than a truncated tool response.

Reopen the receiving host and inspect the same editions, runs, decisions and
asset digests. Restarting the client does not repeat capture or import.

## Node API and merchant MCP

Installed Node import:

```js
import {
  StacWorkspaceClient,
  nativeStacItemId,
  saveStacFile
} from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/buyer/stac/workspace-client';

const client = new StacWorkspaceClient({
  consoleUrlFile: '/private/stac-host.json'
});
try {
  const { workspace } = await client.state();
  const edition = workspace.editions[0];
  const view = await client.edition(edition.id);
  const firstItemId = nativeStacItemId(view.items[0]);
  console.log({ workspaceId: workspace.id, editionId: edition.id, firstItemId });
  await saveStacFile(client, {
    kind: 'report', editionId: edition.id, format: 'csv'
  }, '/private/imagery-review.csv');
} finally {
  client.close();
}
```

The public declaration file describes native query, edition, item, job,
comparison, decision, file and connection contracts. `client.file()` returns
complete original file bytes and their digest. `client.wait()` polls one native
job with cancellation and a timeout; it never dispatches another acquisition.

Initialize the existing merchant MCP server against the same connection:

```sh
starforge merchant-mcp init-stac-workspaces \
  --dir /private/stac-mcp \
  --connection /private/stac-connection.json

starforge merchant-mcp-stdio --config /private/stac-mcp/merchant-mcp.json
```

An existing merchant configuration can add
`"stacWorkspaceConnection": "/private/stac-connection.json"`.
The original operator tool inventory then includes `merchant_stac_*`.
No additional server or source namespace is required.

| Purpose | Original agent tools |
| --- | --- |
| Connection and saved state | `workspaces`, `status`, `records`, `record`, `operation` |
| Imagery review and capture | `discover`, `query_save`, `search_review`, `search_acquire`, `search_resume`, `search_cancel` |
| Scene and asset work | `edition`, `items`, `item`, `compare`, `asset_review`, `asset_acquire`, `decision_save` |
| Source receiving | `inputs`, `input_inspect`, `input_import` |
| Processing | `processing_status`, `processing_read`, `processing_configure`, `processing_action` |
| Complete files | `file_read`, `asset_range`, `file_release`, `disconnect` |

Every table name uses the `merchant_stac_` prefix. Tool descriptions and
schemas contain the exact original field selections.

`file_read` uses the maintained `RetainedFileReads` implementation. Its first
response returns the original file metadata, digest, `readId` and first base64
chunk. Continue with the same file selection, `readId`, `expectedSha256` and
`nextOffset`. A read snapshots the original export once, so later chunks do
not regenerate a handover. Chunks are at most 196,608 bytes, and the last chunk
automatically releases the snapshot. Use `file_release` when stopping early.
The existing retained reader permits four snapshots totaling 256,000,000 bytes,
with a two-minute idle lifetime.

For large original assets, `merchant_stac_asset_range` reads up to 196,608
bytes directly from the native range endpoint. Each response includes the full
asset SHA256/byte length and the chunk SHA256. Pass the full original
`expectedSha256` on every range after the first and verify the full digest after
assembling all chunks. This uses no retained whole-file snapshot or new asset
store. The CLI `download --kind asset` performs streaming and complete-digest
verification automatically.

Buffered JSON response/download limits default to 128 MiB and can be explicitly configured
up to 512 MiB. The original host separately reports its request byte limit; the
client checks it before transmitting complete imports. For an imagery handover
larger than the native HTTP/retained-reader limit, use the original STAC edition
directory or portable receiving command described in the native guide. Its
source files and validation remain the same.

The source-owned distribution registration is
`stac-workspace-agent`. Inspect it with
`starforge registrations --source stac-workspace-agent`; the builder includes
the original client, CLI, types, guide and MCP implementation in the cumulative
merchant package.
